where: Section 1 and Exam traps, third trap
problem: The rule is stated as a hard OpenCL rule: 'global size must be a multiple of local size' and 'local size must divide global size'. That is true for OpenCL 1.x, but OpenCL 2.0 and later allow non-uniform work-groups, where the last group may be smaller (if the device supports it). A student may quote the absolute rule and lose marks on a modern-OpenCL question.
fix: Say: 'In OpenCL 1.x, and in the simple launches used in this course, global size must be a multiple of local size, otherwise the launch fails with an error. OpenCL 2.0+ can allow a smaller last work-group (non-uniform work-groups).' Keep the trap, but word it as a rule of OpenCL 1.x and of the simple launches here.

problem: The table lists only two of the eight work-items (group 1, local ids 2 and 3). A student reading a 'dry run' expects every work-item, and it is not clear why group 0 and local ids 0 and 1 are missing.
fix: Either show all 8 rows (group 0 with local ids 0-3 giving global ids 0-3, then group 1 with local ids 0-3 giving global ids 4-7), or add a line before the table: 'Only the rows needed for C[6] and for the last work-item are shown; group 0 and local ids 0-1 give C[0] to C[5] the same way.'
